# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 84 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 84 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_084_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Chapter 1

**1** After I had written down the commandments and similitudes of the shepherd, the angel of repentance, he came to me and said, "I wish to show you all the things that the Holy Spirit spoke with you in the form of the church, for that Spirit is the Son of God. **2** For since you were weak in the flesh, it was not declared to you through an angel; rather it was declared through the church, so that you might see it vividly and not be frightened, as would happen at the sight of an angel." **3** He showed me, in the Spirit, a great white rock rising up from a plain; and the rock was higher than the mountains, four-cornered, and large enough to contain the whole world. **4** Now the rock was ancient, and a gate had been cut into it — but the gate appeared to me to have been cut recently, and it shone more brightly than the sun, so that I marveled at its brilliance. **5** Around the gate stood twelve virgins; the four who stood at the corners seemed to me mightier than the rest, though all the virgins were glorious; and they stood at the four angles of the gate. **6** Ten other virgins were stationed between them, placed in order along the sides. **7** And there were young men stationed before the gate, about twenty in number, vigorous and stout in bearing. **8** The gate was open, and I saw within the gate large square white stones being fitted together for a tower on both sides of the gate. **9** Above the gate a tower was being built, exceedingly glorious and magnificent, appearing as though made of a single stone. This stone was so clear that it appeared to me more beautiful than the whiteness of snow.

---

### Translator's Note
Similitude 9 is the theological and literary summit of the entire Shepherd of Hermas — the longest and most elaborate section. The rock (v. 3) is later identified as the Son of God (ch. 86); the gate cut into it is also the Son of God, the only way of entry. The tower being built on and through this rock is the Church. The twelve virgins represent virtues as in Sim. 8 ch. 6. SOPHIA follows LOGOS throughout; PNEUMA's "speechless" in v. 4 is evocative but paraphrastic.
